free_tier.stated: USD 2.00/month for Nitro 1 on a 1 Gbps port, printed on the vendor's own LEB page against a struck-through USD 4.00: 1 vCPU on an AMD EPYC 75F3, 2 GB RAM, 30 GB NVMe. Nitro 2 is USD 4.00/month for 2 vCPU, 4 GB, 50 GB. The Ryzen 9 9950X3D line is USD 2.50/month for Ultra 1 (1 vCPU, 2 GB, 30 GB) and USD 5.00 for Ultra 2 (2 vCPU, 4 GB, 50 GB). The LEB offer post prices the same Nitro 1 differently: USD 21.99 for the first year (USD 1.83/month) and USD 43.99/year on renewal (USD 3.67/month), and it tells a buyer to pick a longer billing term at checkout so that coupon LEB50 halves that whole first period. Locations Los Angeles, New Jersey and Amsterdam.

egress.terms: no monthly transfer allowance and no overage price are stated on either page read; the plan card prints a 1 Gbps port and nothing else about traffic

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: the vendor page names a VirtFusion control panel and one-click backups; no API, rclone backend or CLI is documented on the page read
chaining: USD 2.00/month for 2 GB and 30 GB on an EPYC 75F3 with a 1 Gbps port is one of the lowest 2 GB rates, and Los Angeles plus New Jersey plus Amsterdam on one account makes it a candidate for a small always-on worker near the bytes it fetches the missing traffic figure is the reason to test before committing a crawler to it

limits.value: no monthly byte allowance appears on either page read, so nothing volume-shaped is binding: the 1 Gbps port is the only stated limit and throughput is therefore the wall. That is an inference from the plan card, which prints 'Network 1 Gbps' and no traffic figure, and not a vendor statement about shaping.
